title: Hanuma recounts to Bharata about Rama in the forest
introduction: Hanuma recounts to Bharata, broad details relating to the soujourn of Rama, Seetha and Lakshmana in the forest from the day Bharata takes wooden sandals of Rama, till the day Ravana is killed.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे षड्विंशत्यधिकशततमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 126th chapter in Yuddha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
बहूनि नाम वर्षाणि गतस्य सुमहद्वनम् |
शृणोम्यहं प्रीतिकरं मम नाथस्य कीर्तनम्
verses.iast:
bahUni nāma varṣāṇi gatasya sumahadvanam |
śṛṇomyahaṃ prItikaraṃ mama nāthasya kIrtanam
verses.translation: "I am indeed hearing a delight mention of my lord, who proceeded to the vast forest so many years ago.

verses.devanagari:
कल्याणी बत गाथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मे |
एति जीवन्तमानन्दो नरं वर्षशतादपि
verses.iast:
kalyāṇI bata gātheyaṃ laukikI pratibhāti me |
eti jIvantamānando naraṃ varṣaśatādapi
verses.translation: "This common saying sounds to me good, that bliss comes to a surviving man, even if it be after a hundred years!"

glosses.meaning: even if it be after a hundred years!.

verses.devanagari:
राघवस्य हरीणां च कथमासीत्समागमः |
कस्मिन्देशे किमाश्रित्य तत्त्वमाख्याहि पृच्छतः
verses.iast:
rāghavasya harIṇāṃ ca kathamāsItsamāgamaḥ |
kasmindeśe kimāśritya tattvamākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ
verses.translation: "How and on what ground, an alliance has been concluded between Rama and the monkeys and at what place? Tell the truth to me, enquiring as I am."

verses.devanagari:
स पृष्टो राजपुत्रेण बृस्यां समुपवेशितः |
आचचक्षे ततः सर्वं रामस्य चरितं वने
verses.iast:
sa pṛṣṭo rājaputreṇa bṛsyāṃ samupaveśitaḥ |
ācacakṣe tataḥ sarvaṃ rāmasya caritaṃ vane
verses.translation: Seated comfortably on a cushion and interrogated by Bharata, Hanuma thereupon began to narrate the entire exploits of Rama in the forest.

verses.devanagari:
यथा प्रव्रजितो रामो मातुर्दत्ते वरे तव |
यथा च पुत्रशोकेन राजा दशरथो मृतः
यथा दूतैस्त्वमानीतस्तूर्णं राजगृहात्प्रभो |
त्वयायोध्यां प्रविष्टेन यथा राज्यं न चेप्सितम्
चित्रकूटं गिरिं गत्वा राज्येनामित्रकर्शनः |
निमन्त्रितस्त्वया भ्राता धर्ममाचरिता सताम्
स्थितेन राज्ञो वचने यथा राज्यं विसर्जितम् |
आर्यस्य पादुके गृह्य यथासि पुनरागतः
सर्वमेतन्महाबाहो यथावद्विदितं तव |
त्वयि प्रतिप्रयाते तु यद्वृत्तं तन्निबोध मे
verses.iast:
yathā pravrajito rāmo māturdatte vare tava |
yathā ca putraśokena rājā daśaratho mṛtaḥ
yathā dUtaistvamānItastUrṇaṃ rājagṛhātprabho |
tvayāyodhyāṃ praviṣṭena yathā rājyaṃ na cepsitam
citrakUṭaṃ giriṃ gatvā rājyenāmitrakarśanaḥ |
nimantritastvayā bhrātā dharmamācaritā satām
sthitena rāGYo vacane yathā rājyaṃ visarjitam |
āryasya pāduke gṛhya yathāsi punarāgataḥ
sarvametanmahābāho yathāvadviditaṃ tava |
tvayi pratiprayAte tu yadvṛttaṃ tannibodha me
verses.translation: "O Lord, the long-armed! How your mother was conferred with two boons by your father, how Rama was sent to exile, how Dasaratha the king died, with a shocking sorrow for his son's exile, how you were brought quickly from Rajagriha (the seat of government of Kekaya kings) by the envoys, how sovereignty was not coveted by you when you returned to Ayodhya, how on your going to mount Chitrakuta, your, elder brother the tormentator of enemies was invited by you who followed righteousness to take back the kingdom, how Rama who stood by his father's words, renounced the kingdom and stood by his father's words, renounced the kingdom and how your returned to Ayodhya, taking with you the wooden sandals all this is known accurately to you. Hear from me now, that which occurred after you had returned to Ayodhya."

glosses.meaning: to Mount Chitrakuta bhraataa = Rama your elder brother
Rama who stood by the king's words

verses.devanagari:
अपयाते त्वयि तदा समुद्भ्रान्तमृगद्विजम् |
प्रविवेशाथ विजनं सुमहद्दण्डकावनम्
verses.iast:
apayāte tvayi tadā samudbhrāntamṛgadvijam |
praviveśātha vijanaṃ sumahaddaṇḍakāvanam
verses.translation: "When you had gone away, that forest (of Chitrakuta) then assumed a very miserable appearance, with the frightened animals and birds (on seeing strange people there)."

glosses.meaning: then atyartham paridyuunam iva = a very miserable appearance
with the frightened animals and birds ( on seeing strange people in the forest).

verses.devanagari:
तद्धस्तिमृदितं घोरं सिंहवाग्रमृगाकुलम् |
प्रविवेशाथ विजनं स महद्दण्डकावनम्
verses.iast:
taddhastimṛditaṃ ghoraṃ siṃhavāgramṛgākulam |
praviveśātha vijanaṃ sa mahaddaṇḍakāvanam
verses.translation: "Rama, thereupon, entered that large, terrific and solitary forest of Dandaka, which had been trampled by elephants and extensive with lions, tigers and deers."

glosses.meaning: which had been trampled by elephants

verses.devanagari:
तेषां पुरस्ताद्बलवान्गच्छतां गहने वने |
विनदन्सुमहानादं विराधः प्रत्यदृश्यत
verses.iast:
teṣāṃ purastādbalavāngacchatāṃ gahane vane |
vinadansumahānādaṃ virādhaḥ pratyadṛśyata
verses.translation: "In front of them, even as they were going in that dense forest, there appeared Viradha, a demon, uttering forth a very loud roar.

verses.devanagari:
तमुत्क्षिप्य महानादमूर्ध्वबाहुमधोमुखम् |
निखाते प्रक्षिपन्ति स्म नदन्तमिव कुञ्जरम्
verses.iast:
tamutkṣipya mahānādamUrdhvabāhumadhomukham |
nikhāte prakṣipanti sma nadantamiva kuñjaram
verses.translation: "They cast him, who rushed with uplifted arms towards them, into a pit, turning his head bent low, and who was emitting a loud cry, like an elephant."

glosses.meaning: who rushed with uplifted arms towards them
and who was emitting a loud cry

verses.devanagari:
तत्कृत्वा दुष्करं कर्म भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ |
सायाह्ने शरभङ्गस्य रम्यमाश्रममीयतुः
verses.iast:
tatkṛtvā duṣkaraṃ karma bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau |
sāyāhne śarabhañgasya ramyamāśramamIyatuḥ
verses.translation: "Carrying out that ardous task, Rama and Lakshmana, both the brothers, went to the beautiful hermitage of Sharbhanga, in that evening.

verses.devanagari:
शरभङ्गे दिवं प्राप्ते रामः सत्यपराक्रमः |
अभिवाद्य मुनीन्सर्वाञ्जनस्थानमुपागमत्
verses.iast:
śarabhañge divaṃ prāpte rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ |
abhivādya munInsarvāñjanasthānamupāgamat
verses.translation: "Offering salutation to all the hermits when Sharabhanga ascended to heaven, Rama who truly mighty, reached the region of Janasthana."

verses.devanagari:
पश्चाच्चूर्पणखा नाम रामपार्श्वमुपागता |
ततो रामेण संदिष्टो लक्ष्मणः सहसोत्थितः
प्रगृह्य खड्गं चिच्छेद कर्णनासे महाबलः |
verses.iast:
paścāccūrpaṇakhā nāma rāmapārśvamupāgatā |
tato rāmeṇa sandiṣṭo lakṣmaṇaḥ sahasotthitaḥ
pragṛhya khaḍgaṃ ciccheda karṇanāse mahābalaḥ |
verses.translation: "Thereafter, a female-demon called Surpanakha sought the presence of Rama. As ordered by Rama, the mighty Lakshmana thereupon rose quickly and seizing a sword, chopped off her ears and nose."

verses.devanagari:
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि रक्षसां भीमकर्मणाम् |
हतानि वसता तत्र राघवेण महात्मना
verses.iast:
caturdaśasahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhImakarmaṇām |
hatāni vasatā tatra rāghaveṇa mahātmanā
verses.translation: "Fourteen thousand demons, inhabiting Janasthana-region, were killed by the great-souled Rama, while sojourning that region."

verses.devanagari:
एकेन सह संगम्य रामेण रणमूर्धनि |
अह्नश्चतुर्थभागेन निःशेषा राक्षसाः कृताः
verses.iast:
ekena saha saṅgamya rāmeṇa raṇamūrdhani |
ahnaścaturthabhāgena niḥśeṣā rākṣasāḥ kṛtāḥ
verses.translation: "The demons, who came together at the battle-front, were wholly finished by Rama alone, in a fraction of a quarter of a day."

glosses.meaning: in a fraction of a quarter of a day.

verses.devanagari:
महाबला महावीर्यास्तपसो विघ्नकारिणः
निहता राघवेणाजौ दण्डकारण्यवासिनः |
verses.iast:
mahābalā mahāvīryāstapaso vighnakāriṇaḥ
nihatā rāghaveṇājau daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinaḥ |
verses.translation: "The demons who were the mighty inhabitants of Dandaka-forest, who were causing obstacles to the austerity of the ascetics, were killed by Rama."

verses.devanagari:
राक्षसाश्च विनिष्पिष्टाः खरश्च निहतो रणे
दूषणं चाग्रतो हत्वा त्रिशिरास्तदनन्तम् |
verses.iast:
rākṣasāśca viniṣpiṣṭāḥ kharaśca nihato raṇe
dūṣaṇaṃ cāgrato hatvā triśirāstadanantam |
verses.translation: "The demons were smashed in the battle. Khara (their leader) also was killed. After killing Dushana (his brother) first, Trishira (the other brother) was killed thereafter."

verses.devanagari:
ततस्तेनार्दिता बाला रावणं समुपागता
रावणानुचरो घोरो मारीचो नाम राक्षसः |
लोभयामास वैदेहीं भूत्वा रत्नमयो मृगः
verses.iast:
tatastenārditā bālā rāvaṇaṃ samupāgatā
rāvaṇānucaro ghoro mārīco nāma rākṣasaḥ |
lobhayāmāsa vaidehīṃ bhūtvā ratnamayo mṛgaḥ
verses.translation: "Tormented by the incident of destruction of demons, the foolish Surpanakha sought refuge with Ravana. Disguised in the form of a deer studded with precious stones, a terrific demon by name, Maricha, a follower of Ravana, allured Seetha."

glosses.meaning: in the form of a deer

verses.devanagari:
सा राममब्रवीद्दृष्ट्वा वैदेही गृह्यतामिति |
अयं मनोहरह् कान्त आश्रमो नो भविष्यति
verses.iast:
sā rāmamabravīddṛṣṭvā vaidehī gṛhyatāmiti |
ayaṃ manoharah kānta āśramo no bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "That Seetha, on seeing it, told Rama, 'Let this deer be caught. Our hermitage will turn out to be charming and pleasing to the eye'."

verses.devanagari:
ततो रामो धनुष्पाणिर्धावन्तमनुधावति |
स तं जघान धावन्तं शरेणानतपर्वणा
verses.iast:
tato rāmo dhanuṣpāṇirdhāvantamanudhāvati |
sa taṃ jaghāna dhāvantaṃ śareṇānataparvaṇā
verses.translation: "Thereupon, Rama wielding a bow in his arm, chased that deer and killed that running one, with an arrow of curved knots."

verses.devanagari:
अथ सौम्या दशग्रीवो मृगं याते तु राघवे |
लक्ष्मणे चापि निष्क्रान्ते प्रविवेशाश्रमं तदा
verses.iast:
atha saumyā daśagrIvo mṛgaṃ yāte tu rāghave |
lakṣmaṇe cāpi niṣkrānte praviveśāśramaṃ tadā
verses.translation: "O good sir! While Rama was chasing the deer and even when Lakshmana had gone out, Ravana forthwith entered their hermitage during that interval."

verses.devanagari:
जग्राह तरसा सीतां ग्रहः खे रोहिणीम् इव |
त्रातुकामं ततो युद्धे हत्वा गृध्रं जटायुषम्
प्रगृह्य सहसा सीतां जगामाशु स राक्षसः |
verses.iast:
jagrāha tarasā sItāṃ grahaḥ khe rohiṇIm iva |
trātukāmaṃ tato yuddhe hatvā gṛdhraṃ jaṭāyuṣam
pragṛhya sahasā sItāṃ jagāmāśu sa rākṣasaḥ |
verses.translation: "Ravana, the demon, seized Seetha, even as a planet like Mars would obscure the constellation, Rohini. Having killed a vulture named Jatayu, who sought to deliver her, Ravana then went quickly in haste, taking Seetha with him"

glosses.meaning: even as a planet like Mars would obscure the constellation

verses.devanagari:
ततस्त्वद्भुतसङ्काशाः स्थिताः पर्वतमूर्धनि
सीतां गृहीत्वा गच्छन्तं वानराः पर्वतोपमाः |
ददृशुर्विस्मितास्तत्र रावणं राक्षसाधिपम्
verses.iast:
tatastvadbhutasañkāśāḥ sthitāḥ parvatamUrdhani
sItāṃ gṛhItvā gacchantaṃ vānarāḥ parvatopamāḥ |
dadṛśurvismitāstatra rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam
verses.translation: "Then, in surprise, some monkeys who was staying on a mountain-peak, looking like mountain, saw, with astonishment writ large in their faces, Ravana the king of demons, passing that way, taking away Seetha."

glosses.meaning: who were staying on a mountain-peak
with astonishment writ large in their faces

verses.devanagari:
ततः शीघ्रतरं गत्वा तद्विमानं मनोजवम् |
आरुह्य सह वैदेह्या पुष्पकं स महाबलः
प्रविवेर्श तदा लङ्कां रावणो लोकरावणः |
verses.iast:
tataḥ śīghrataraṃ gatvā tadvimānaṃ manojavam |
āruhya saha vaidehyā puṣpakaṃ sa mahābalaḥ
praviverśa tadā lañkāṃ rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ |
verses.translation: "Going still faster and ascending along with Seetha, the aerial car, Pushpaka, which was as swift as thought, the mighty Ravana the king of demons thereupon entered the City of Lanka."

glosses.meaning: which was as swift as thought

verses.devanagari:
तां सुवर्णपरिक्रान्ते शुभे महति वेश्मनि
प्रवेश्य मैथिलीं वाक्यैः सान्त्वयामास रावणः |
verses.iast:
tāṃ suvarṇaparikrānte śubhe mahati veśmani
praveśya maithilIṃ vākyaiḥ sāntvayāmāsa rāvaṇaḥ |
verses.translation: "Conducting that Seetha into a large beautiful mansion, embellished with gold, that Ravana sought to cajole her gently with his words."

verses.devanagari:
तृणवद्भाषितं तस्य तं च नैरृतपुंगवम्
अचिन्तयन्ती वैदेही ह्यशोकवनिकां गता |
verses.iast:
tṛṇavadbhāṣitaṃ tasya taṃ ca nairṛtapuṅgavam
acintayantī vaidehī hyaśokavanikāṃ gatā |
verses.translation: "Caring a straw for that Ravana and his talk, Seetha, later, actually remained in Ashoka-grove."

glosses.meaning: even as a blade of grass

verses.devanagari:
न्यवर्तत तदा रामो मृगं हत्वा तदा वने
निवर्तमानः काकुत्स्थो दृष्ट्वा गृध्रं प्रविव्यथे |
गृध्रं हतं तदा दग्ध्वा रामः प्रियसखं पितुः
verses.iast:
nyavartata tadā rāmo mṛgaṃ hatvā tadā vane
nivartamānaḥ kākutstho dṛṣṭvā gṛdhraṃ pravivyathe |
gṛdhraṃ hataṃ tadā dagdhvā rāmaḥ priyasakhaṃ pituḥ
verses.translation: "Having killed that deer, Rama while returning to the hermitage, saw the vulture (Jatayu) in the forest. Rama was greatly disturbed. Seeing the vulture (Jatayu) who was dearer to him than his own father killed, Rama was disturbed."

verses.devanagari:
मार्गमाणस्तु वैदेहीं राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः |
गोदावरीमनुचरन्वनोद्देशांश्च पुष्पितान्
verses.iast:
mārgamāṇastu vaidehīṃ rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ |
godāvarImanucaranvanoddeśāṃśca puṣpitān
verses.translation: "While searching for Seetha, RAma along with Lakshmana strolled after blossomed woodlands along the bank of Godavari-river."

verses.devanagari:
आसेदतुर्महारण्ये कबन्धं नाम राक्षसं |
ततः कबन्धवचनाद्रामः सत्यपराक्रमः
ऋश्यमूकं गिरिं गत्वा सुग्रीवेण समागतः |
verses.iast:
āsedaturmahāraṇye kabandhaṃ nāma rākṣasaṃ |
tataḥ kabandhavacanādrāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ
ṛśyamUkaṃ giriṃ gatvā sugrIveṇa samāgataḥ |
verses.translation: "They met, in that great forest, a demon by name Kabandha. Then according to the advice of Kabandha, Rama of true prowess met Sugreeva, after heading for Mount Rishyamuka."

glosses.meaning: according to the advice of Kabandha

verses.devanagari:
तयोः समागमः पूर्वं प्रीत्या हार्दो व्यजायत
इतरेतर संवादात्प्रगाढः प्रणयस्तयोः |
इतरेतरसंवादात्प्रगाढः प्रणयस्तयोः
verses.iast:
tayoḥ samāgamaḥ pUrvaṃ prItyā hārdo vyajāyata
itaretara saṃvādātpragāḍhaḥ praṇayastayoḥ |
itaretarasaṃvādātpragāḍhaḥ praṇayastayoḥ
verses.translation: "Even before they met, a meeting of hearts through affinity, had taken place between them. Sugreeva had been banished in the past by the enraged Vali, his elder brother and as a result of mutual talks, affection deeply arose between Rama and Sugreeva."

glosses.meaning: a meeting of hearts through affinity
and as a result of mutual talks

verses.devanagari:
रामः स्वबाहुवीर्येण स्वराज्यं प्रत्यपादयत् |
वालिनं समरे हत्वा महाकायं महाबलम्
verses.iast:
rāmaḥ svabāhuvIryeṇa svarājyaṃ pratyapādayat |
vālinaṃ samare hatvā mahākāyaṃ mahābalam
verses.translation: "Having killed with the strength of his arms in combat, the mighty Vali with a colossal body, Rama caused the kingdom of Sugreeva restored.

glosses.meaning: with the strength of his arms
caused his own kingdom restored (to Sugreeva).

verses.devanagari:
सुग्रीवः स्थापितो राज्ये सहितः सर्ववानरैः |
रामाय प्रतिजानीते राजपुत्र्यास्तु मार्गणम्
verses.iast:
sugrIvaḥ sthāpito rājye sahitaḥ sarvavānaraiḥ |
rāmāya pratijānIte rājaputryāstu mārgaṇam
verses.translation: "Sugreeva, who was established in his kingdom with all, his monkeys, had given his pledge to Rama, to commence a search for Seetha the princess."

glosses.meaning: who was established in his kingdom

verses.devanagari:
आदिष्टा वानरेन्द्रेण सुग्रीवेण महात्मना |
दशकोट्यः प्लवङ्गानां सर्वाः प्रस्थापिता दिशः
verses.iast:
ādiṣṭā vānarendreṇa sugrIveṇa mahātmanā |
daśakoṭyaḥ plavañgānāṃ sarvāḥ prasthāpitā diśaḥ
verses.translation: "Ten crores of monkeys were accordingly commanded by the great-souled Sugreeva and sent to all the four quarters."

glosses.meaning: were sent sarvaaH dishaH = to all the four quarter.

verses.devanagari:
तेषां नो विप्रनष्टानां विन्ध्ये पर्वतसत्तमे |
भृशं शोकाभितप्तानां महान्कालोअत्यवर्तत
verses.iast:
teṣāṃ no vipranaṣṭānāṃ vindhye parvatasattame |
bhṛśaṃ śokābhitaptānāṃ mahānkāloatyavartata
verses.translation: "Having lost our way in Vindhya, the foremost of mountain-ranges, a long time slipped past us and we felt sore-stricken with sorrow."

glosses.meaning: and we felt sore stricken with sorrow.

verses.devanagari:
भ्राता तु गृध्रराजस्य सम्पातिर्नाम वीर्यवान् |
समाख्याति स्म वसतिं सीताया रावणालये
verses.iast:
bhrātā tu gṛdhrarājasya sampātirnāma vIryavān |
samākhyāti sma vasatiṃ sItāyā rāvaṇālaye
verses.translation: "Meanwhile, the brother of Jatayu (the king of vultures), Sampati by name, precisely communicated to us that Seetha was dwelling in the habitation of Ravana."

verses.devanagari:
सोअहं दुःखपरीतानां दुःखं तज्ज्ञातिनां नुदन् |
आत्मवीर्यं समास्थाय योजनानां शतं प्लुतः
verses.iast:
soahaṃ duḥkhaparItānāṃ duḥkhaṃ tajGYātināṃ nudan |
ātmavIryaṃ samāsthāya yojanānāṃ śataṃ plutaḥ
verses.translation: "Removing the grief of my kinsfolk, who were seized with sorrow, I, as such, crossed one hundred yojanas (eight hundred miles of the ocean), resorting to my own strength."

verses.devanagari:
तत्राहमेकामद्राक्षमशोकवनिकां गताम् |
कौशेयवस्त्रां मलिनां निरानन्दां दृढव्रताम्
verses.iast:
tatrāhamekāmadrākṣamaśokavanikāṃ gatām |
kauśeyavastrāṃ malināṃ nirānandāṃ dṛḍhavratām
verses.translation: "There, I saw Seetha, living alone in a grove of Ashoka trees, clad in a soiled silk-saree, looking cheerless, but unflinching in her vow."

glosses.meaning: unflinching as she was in her vow

verses.devanagari:
तया समेत्य विधिवत्पृष्ट्वा सर्वमनिन्दिताम् |
अभिज्ञानं मया दत्तं रामनामाङ्गुलीयकम्
verses.iast:
tayā sametya vidhivatpṛṣṭvā sarvamaninditām |
abhijJṇānaṃ mayā dattaṃ rāmanāmāṇ^gulīyakam
verses.translation: "After meeting her and duly enquiring that faultless Seetha, everything of her, a ring with the name, Rama engraved on it, was handed-over to her by me as a token."

verses.devanagari:
अभिज्ञानं मणिं लब्ध्वा चरितार्थोअहमागतः |
मया च पुनरागम्य रामस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः
अभिज्ञानं मया दत्तमर्चिष्मान्स महामणिः |
verses.iast:
abhiGYānaṃ maṇiṃ labdhvā caritārthoahamāgataḥ |
mayā ca punarāgamya rāmasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ
abhiGYānaṃ mayā dattamarciṣmānsa mahāmaṇiḥ |
verses.translation: "Receiving in return from her, a jewel (from her head), I came back to the northern shore, successful as I was in my undertaking. On my return, that brilliant and valuable jewel was given by me as a token to Rama who was unweary in action."

glosses.meaning: as a token (in return from her)
I came (to the northern sea shore)
successful as I was in my undertaking

verses.devanagari:
श्रुत्वा तां मैथिलीं हृष्टस्त्वाशशंसे स जीवितम्
जीवितान्तमनुप्राप्तः पीत्वामृतमिवातुरः |
verses.iast:
śrutvā tāṃ maithilIṃ hṛṣṭastvāśaśaṃse sa jIvitam
jIvitāntamanuprāptaḥ pItvAmṛtamivāturaḥ |
verses.translation: "On hearing the news of Seetha, Rama for his part regained the hope to survive, as a dying patient would, on drinking the ambrosia."

verses.devanagari:
उद्योजयिष्यन्नुद्योगं दध्रे लङ्कावधे मनः
जिघांसुरिव लोकांस्ते सर्वांल्लोकान्विभावसुः |
verses.iast:
udyojayiṣyannudyogaṃ dadhre lañkāvadhe manaḥ
jighāṃsuriva lokāṃste sarvāṃllokānvibhāvasuḥ |
verses.translation: "Excited as he was to put forth a war-effort, he set his mind on the destruction of Lanka, as the fire-god intending to destroy all the three worlds, would, at the end of the universe."

glosses.meaning: at the end of the universe.

verses.devanagari:
ततः समुद्रमासाद्य नलं सेतुमकारयत्
अतरत्कपिवीराणां वाहिनी तेन सेतुना |
verses.iast:
tataḥ samudramāsādya nalaṃ setumakārayat
ataratkapivIrāṇāṃ vāhinI tena setunā |
verses.translation: "Then, on reaching the ocean, he got a bridge constructed by Nala and through that bridge, the army of the valiant monkeys crossed the ocean."

glosses.meaning: the army of the valiant monkeys

verses.devanagari:
प्रहस्तमवधीन्नीलः कुम्भकर्णं तु राघवः
लक्ष्मणो रावणसुतं स्वयं रामस्तु रावणम् |
verses.iast:
prahastamavadhInnIlaḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ tu rāghavaḥ
lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇasutaṃ svayaṃ rāmastu rāvaṇam |
verses.translation: "Neela killed Prahasta. Rama, the scion of Raghu dynasty, personally killed Kumbhakarna and Ravana. Lakshmana killed Indrajit, the son of Ravana."

verses.devanagari:
स शक्रेण समागम्य यमेन वरुणेन च
महेश्वरस्वयम्भूभ्यां तथा दशरथेन च |
तैश्च काकुत्थ्सो वरान् लेभे परंतपः
सुरर्षिभिश्च काकुत्स्थो वरांल्लेभे परन्तपः |
verses.iast:
sa śakreṇa samāgamya yamena varuṇena ca
maheśvarasvayambhūbhyāṃ tathā daśarathena ca |
taiśca kākutthso varān lebhe parantapaḥ
surarṣibhiśca kākutstho varāṃllebhe parantapaḥ |
verses.translation: "The illustrious Rama, the destroyer of enemies, happened to meet Indra the lord of celestials, Yama the lord of dissolution, Varuna the lord of waters, Maheshvara, the great lord (Shiva), Brahma the lord of creation as also Dasaratha (his deceased father) and was bestowed boons by them. Sages and celestial masters who came there, too gave boons."

verses.devanagari:
स तु दत्तवरः प्रीत्या वानरैश्च समागतः
पुष्पकेण विमानेन किष्किन्धामभ्युपागमत् |
verses.iast:
sa tu dattavaraḥ prItyā vānaraiśca samāgataḥ
puṣpakeṇa vimānena kiṣkindhāmabhyupāgamat |
verses.translation: "Having been granted boons, Rama for his part flew to Kishkindha in an aerial car called Pushpaka, along with the monkeys who gathered there."

verses.devanagari:
तं गङ्गां पुनरासाद्य वसन्तं मुनिसंनिधौ
अविघ्नं पुष्ययोगेन श्वो रामं द्रष्टुमर्हसि |
verses.iast:
taṃ gañgāṃ punarāsādya vasantaṃ munisaṃnidhau
avighnaṃ puṣyayogena śvo rāmaṃ draṣṭumarhasi |
verses.translation: "Reaching the coast-line of Ganga-river again, Rama is staying in the presence of the sage, Bharadwaja. Tomorrow, when the moon will be in conjunction with the asteroid, Pushya you will be able to see Rama, without any obstacle."

glosses.meaning: in the presence of the sage
when the moon will be in conjunction with asteroid

verses.devanagari:
ततः स सत्यं हनुमद्वचो महन् |
निशम्य हृष्टो भरतः कृताञ्जलिः |
उवाच वाणीं मनसः प्रहर्षिणी |
चिरस्य पूर्णः खलु मे मनोरथः
verses.iast:
tataḥ sa satyaṃ hanumadvaco mahan |
niśamya hṛṣṭo bharataḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ |
uvāca vāṇIṃ manasaḥ praharṣiṇI |
cirasya pUrṇaḥ khalu me manorathaḥ
verses.translation: "Gladdened to hear Rama's impending return to Ayodhya in the sweet words of Hanuma, Bharata offered his salutation by joining his palms together and spoke the following words, which enraptured his mind: 'My desire has been fulfilled indeed after a long time'."

glosses.meaning: and offering his salutation to him by joining his palms together
